cleanIntro:
This guide follows CMMG's Dissent owner's manual; check your variant against it. The Dissent is a compact-action rifle: the upper and lower still part on an AR-style pivot pin and takedown pin, but there is no buffer tube. The bolt carrier, its two action springs, the guide rods, the backplate and a bumper ride together in the upper as one action assembly, and the charging handle pushes the whole assembly out of the back of the upper.

CMMG's book takes that action assembly apart down to the bolt and the extractor, and stops there. It writes two cam-pin procedures, one for DI rifles and one for RDB rifles, and does not say which one your Dissent is.

steps.title: Selector on SAFE — the hammer must be cocked
steps.action: This guide follows CMMG's Dissent owner's manual; check your variant against it. Keep the muzzle in a safe direction for the whole procedure and put the selector on SAFE. The selector will only go to SAFE when the hammer is cocked.
steps.prose: If the selector will not turn to SAFE, the hammer has already fallen. Do not force the lever.
steps.quote: Place your selector on “SAFE”. You cannot select “SAFE” unless the hammer is cocked.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — UNLOADING and CLEARING YOUR FIREARM, PDF p.1

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine catch button and pull the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out before the charging handle moves. Cycling the action with a loaded magazine in just chambers the next round.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine catch button and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — UNLOADING and CLEARING YOUR FIREARM, PDF p.2

steps.title: Charging handle back — the chambered round drops out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back until it stops. Any round in the chamber is extracted and ejected. Let it fall to the ground; do not try to catch it.
steps.prose: Count on a round being there until you have looked.
steps.quote: Eject the chambered cartridge by retracting the charging handle until it stops. Let the ejected cartridge fall to the ground.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — UNLOADING and CLEARING YOUR FIREARM, PDF p.2

steps.title: Lock the bolt open on the BOTTOM of the bolt catch
steps.action: With the charging handle held back, press the bottom of the bolt catch to lock the bolt open. If you cannot work the charging handle and the bolt catch at the same time, an empty magazine will trip the catch for you.
steps.prose: The bottom of the catch locks the bolt. Pressing the top releases it.
steps.quote: Lock the bolt open by depressing the bottom of the bolt catch.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — UNLOADING and CLEARING YOUR FIREARM, PDF p.2

steps.title: Charging handle forward until it clicks
steps.action: With the bolt held open on the catch, push the charging handle forward until it clicks and re-latches.
steps.prose: The bolt stays back. Only the handle goes home.
steps.quote: Push the charging handle forward until it clicks to re-latch the charging handle.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — UNLOADING and CLEARING YOUR FIREARM, PDF p.2

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber and the receiver
steps.action: Look into the chamber and the receiver and confirm there is no cartridge anywhere in the action.
steps.prose: Seeing an empty chamber is the check. Working the action is not.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and receiver to ensure you have removed all cartridges from the action.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — UNLOADING and CLEARING YOUR FIREARM, PDF p.2

steps.title: Check it again, then bolt and carrier back into battery
steps.action: Check again that the rifle is unloaded, then let the bolt and carrier go forward into battery.
steps.prose: The upper opens with the action closed.
steps.quote: Reverify your rifle is unloaded and return the bolt and carrier into battery.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

steps.title: Both pins: push partway in from the LEFT
steps.action: From the left side, push the rear takedown pin and the front pivot pin partway in, just far enough that the detents no longer hold them closed. A delrin takedown-pin punch helps if they are stiff.
steps.prose: Partway only. Both pins stay in the receiver.
steps.quote: Partially push the rear take down pin and the front pivot pin from left so they are not captured by the detents that retain them in the receiver in the closed position.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

steps.title: Rear takedown pin out to the RIGHT, to its open detent
steps.action: Pull the rear takedown pin the rest of the way out to the right side of the lower until it catches on the detent that holds it open.
steps.prose: The pin stops at the detent. Do not pull it past.
steps.quote: Pull the rear take down pin the rest of the way to the right side of the lower receiver until it engages the detent that holds the pin in the open position.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

steps.title: Pivot the lower away from the upper
steps.action: Swing the lower receiver away from the upper on the front pivot pin.
steps.prose: The two halves are still joined at the front pin.
steps.quote: Pivot the lower receiver away from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

steps.title: Front pivot pin out to the RIGHT — the halves separate
steps.action: Pull the front pivot pin the rest of the way out to the right side of the lower until it catches on its open detent. The upper and lower are now apart; set the upper aside.
steps.prose: Same as the rear pin: it stops at the detent.
steps.quote: Pull the front pivot pin the rest of the way to the right side of lower receiver until it engages the detent that holds the pin in the open position.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

steps.title: Charging handle back — the action assembly slides out the rear
steps.action: Pick up the upper and pull the charging handle all the way back. The handle pushes the whole action assembly out of the back of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: On the Dissent the bolt carrier, springs and guide rods come out together. Catch the assembly as it leaves the upper.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle all the way to the rear to push the action assembly out of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the lower receiver, the upper receiver and the action assembly. CMMG's field strip continues into the action assembly: bumper, backplate, action springs, guide rods, anti-bounce weight, firing pin, cam pin, bolt and extractor. All of that is in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: CMMG only calls the rifle field stripped for cleaning once the extractor is out, so its cleaning sections assume you have done the deep steps.
steps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

deepSteps.title: Bumper off — push UP from underneath
deepSteps.action: Push the action assembly's bumper up from underneath to take it off. Set it aside.
deepSteps.prose: The bumper sits against the backplate. It has to come off before the backplate will move.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the action assembly bumper by pushing it up from underneath the action assembly.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

deepSteps.title: Backplate off under spring pressure, then the springs
deepSteps.action: Stand the action assembly bolt side down on a flat surface. Press both action springs down by hand to take their tension off the backplate, slide the backplate off the guide rods, then ease the springs off the guide rods.
deepSteps.prose: ⚠ The two springs are compressed against the backplate. Keep your hand on them until they are fully relaxed.
deepSteps.quote: Place the action assembly bolt-side first down on a flat surface and depress both springs by hand to take the tension off the backplate, which can now slide freely off the guide rods. Carefully remove springs from the guide rods.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.3

deepSteps.title: Guide rods out the FRONT — the anti-bounce weight comes free
deepSteps.action: With the springs off, slide the guide rods forward out of the carrier key. That frees the anti-bounce weight, which lifts off the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Note where the anti-bounce weight sat on the carrier key. It has to go back in the same place.
deepSteps.quote: Once the springs are removed, they should be free to slide forward out of the carrier key. This will also allow the antibounce weight to be removed from the carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out — LEFT side
deepSteps.action: Pull the firing pin retaining pin out of the left side of the bolt carrier group.
deepSteps.prose: It is small. Work over the bench.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the left side of the bolt carrier group.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Bolt face UP — firing pin out the rear
deepSteps.action: Tilt the carrier so the bolt face points up and take the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Bolt face up lets the pin drop back toward you.
deepSteps.quote: Tilt bolt face up and remove firing pin from the rear of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Line up the cam pin — DI and RDB differ
deepSteps.action: CMMG writes this step two ways. On a DI rifle, push the bolt into the carrier until it rotates and stops in the in-battery position; that lines the cam pin up with a recess in the carrier key. On an RDB rifle the carrier key and cam pin are already lined up, and nothing extra is needed.
deepSteps.prose: The book does not say which system your Dissent uses. Check your rifle against the book before you go on.
deepSteps.quote: For DI firearms, push bolt into the carrier until it rotates and comes to a stop (in battery position). This will align the cam pin with a recess in the carrier key for removal. RDB firearms align the carrier key and the cam pin for removal without any additional steps.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Cam pin out — DI and RDB differ
deepSteps.action: On a DI rifle, turn the cam pin 90 degrees and lift it out of the bolt and carrier. On an RDB rifle, use a flat-head screwdriver to pull the head of the cam pin up toward the carrier key, then turn the carrier upside down and tap it gently on a flat surface until the cam pin drops out.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt cannot leave the carrier until the cam pin is out. Gently means gently: tap, do not hammer.
deepSteps.quote: For DI firearms, turn the cam pin 90 degrees and lift it out from the bolt and carrier. For RDB firearms, use a flat head screw driver to pull the head of the cam pin up towards the carrier key. Turn the carrier upside down and gently tap on a flat surface to remove the cam pin from the carrier and bolt.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Bolt out the front of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Pull the bolt forward out of the carrier and set the carrier aside.
deepSteps.prose: Keep this bolt with this rifle. CMMG warns never to swap bolts between rifles.
deepSteps.quote: Pull bolt forward out of carrier. Set the carrier aside.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin out with a punch
deepSteps.action: Drive the extractor pin out of the bolt with a punch. Light pressure on the extractor makes the pin come out more easily.
deepSteps.prose: The pressure takes the spring load off the pin. Without it the pin binds.
deepSteps.quote: With a punch, remove the extractor pin from the bolt assembly. Slight pressure applied to the extractor will ease removal of the extractor pin.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: Extractor off — spring and insert STAY in it
deepSteps.action: Lift the extractor off the bolt. Its spring and elastomer insert should stay captured in the extractor; leave them there.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ CMMG says not to remove the spring and insert from the extractor.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the extractor. The extractor spring and elastomer insert should be captured in the extractor; do not remove the spring and elastomer from the extractor.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

deepSteps.title: This is where CMMG stops
deepSteps.action: The rifle is now field stripped for cleaning as CMMG describes it: lower, upper, bumper, backplate, two action springs, guide rods, anti-bounce weight, carrier, firing pin, firing pin retaining pin, cam pin, bolt, extractor pin and extractor. CMMG's book goes no further.
deepSteps.prose: Anything past this point goes to CMMG or a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: Do not disassemble your firearm any further than described. Any maintenance that requires further disassembly should be performed by CMMG or a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite: CMMG DISSENT — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.4

cleaning.name: UPPER AND BARREL
tasks: Cleaning fluid on the bore and chamber, the gas tube, the upper receiver and barrel, the locking lugs, and anywhere there is powder fouling, corrosion, dirt or dust.
Chamber brush on the cleaning rod, dipped in fluid: push it into the chamber and locking lugs and twist.
Bore brush dipped in fluid: run it through from the chamber out the muzzle device several times.
Swab with fluid from the chamber out the muzzle; let the solvent sit on carbon, then wipe. Run clean swabs through until they come out dry and clean; if they do not, brush and swab again.
Worn bore brush on the outside of the protruding gas tube.
Do not try to remove heat discoloration from the gas tube.
Charging handle: wipe with a solvent-dampened patch, then dry with a cloth.
Inspect the upper for worn, broken or damaged parts.

Light lube on the bore and chamber, the outside of the barrel and the gas block, under the handguard and on the charging handle; one lubricated swab from the receiver to the muzzle. Do not over-lubricate.
Lubricate the locking lugs.

cleaning.name: BOLT AND CARRIER
tasks: ⛔ Never interchange bolts between rifles.
Every part and outer surface of the bolt carrier assembly with a swab soaked in cleaning fluid.
Carrier key: worn bore brush dipped in fluid, then dry with a pipe cleaner.
Locking lugs: brush off carbon and dirt.
Behind the bolt rings and under the lip of the extractor.
Ejector: press it in repeatedly with a punch to clear brass shavings and make sure it moves freely, without damaging the bolt.

Inspect the bolt for cracks, especially around the cam pin hole; the firing pin retaining pin for bends, breaks or dents; the cam pin for cracks or chips; the firing pin for bends, cracks or a chipped or blunted tip.
Lubricate the carrier inside and out, the bolt, cam pin, firing pin and retaining pin, with one drop inside the carrier key. Flush the ejector with lubricant and cycle it so its spring is lubricated.

cleaning.name: LOWER RECEIVER
tasks: Trigger group: brush and/or cotton swab with cleaning fluid to lift dirt and debris.
Lower receiver: same for powder fouling, corrosion and dirt.
Inspect the lower for worn, broken or damaged parts.
Lightly lubricate the lower receiver and its internal parts.

reassembly: Extractor, with its spring and insert, onto the bolt: press it down until its pivot hole lines up with the hole in the bolt, then put the extractor pin in. If the spring came loose, seat its large end in the extractor.
Stagger the bolt rings so the gaps do not line up. Not needed with a one-piece gas ring or on an RDB rifle.
Bolt into the carrier with the extractor claw on the carrier's right side.
Line up the cam pin hole in the bolt with the cam pin slot in the carrier; cam pin in and turn it 90°.
Firing pin into the opening at the rear of the carrier and seat it. Turn the cam pin if needed to let it seat.
Bolt pulled forward, firing pin retaining pin back in. Installed correctly, the firing pin cannot fall or be pulled out.
Anti-bounce weight onto the carrier key; guide rods in from the front of the carrier, keeping the weight seated.
Front of the carrier key down on a flat surface; action springs onto the guide rods.
Press the springs down and slide the backplate onto the grooves at the back of the guide rods. The springs should stay captured. Check the anti-bounce weight is still in place.
Bumper in from the top of the guide rods, pushed against the backplate. The action assembly is complete.
Action assembly into the upper, carrier key lined up; it should slide forward freely and push the charging handle fully forward.
⛔ Hammer cocked and selector on SAFE before the upper goes back on the lower.
Line up the pivot holes and push the front pivot pin in; swing the halves together and push the rear takedown pin in.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber seen empty. Pull the charging handle back and let it go. Selector on SAFE, press the trigger: the hammer must not fall. Selector on FIRE, press the trigger: the hammer falls. Hold the trigger back, cycle the action, then let the trigger go: you should hear a click as the hammer is caught. Press the trigger again: the hammer falls. If the rifle fails any check, look over the reassembly; if it still fails after correct reassembly, contact CMMG or a qualified gunsmith.
